summary: WhatsApp session credentials routed to author's hardcoded MongoDB cluster with Telegram backdoor for author remote control
details: The package pairs WhatsApp accounts via Baileys and persists all authentication artifacts (creds and signal keys) to a hardcoded MongoDB Atlas cluster owned by the author. config/index.js and config.env hardcode `mongodb+srv://unity-free:unity-free@unity-free.pc6vkvw.mongodb.net/` as the fallback when MONGODB_URI is unset; start.js and src/sessionManager.js write every paired user's Baileys credentials there via `UserAuthState.findByIdAndUpdate`. Baileys creds are long-lived WhatsApp account credentials, so any installer running the package with defaults deposits full WhatsApp sessions for themselves and every downstream user paired through the dashboard or Telegram bot into a database whose credentials are shipped in the tarball. Independently, src/telegram/superBot.js runs a Telegram bot using the hardcoded author-owned token `TG_SUPER_BOT_TOKEN` and gates admin commands against hardcoded author admin IDs (`7752365037,6794311904,8778431141`); the admin surface includes `/pair <number>` (invokes session creation), yt-dlp execFile download commands, and management operations, giving the author a remote command channel into every installer's running process via api.telegram.org polling. config.env also ships live Google Gemini, Gmail SMTP, and two Telegram bot credentials that enable those relay/backdoor flows. After a successful pair, autoFollowChannels(userJid) uses the freshly paired user's WhatsApp identity to follow the author's newsletter channels, re-run on a 6-hour cron.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
